site.name: aeroiq
site.summary: AeroIQ Fictional API monitoring and observability SaaS (Datadog / Vercel Observability-style). Pages - `index.html` — Overview dashboard. Left rail nav; top bar with org switcher, environment tabs (Production / Staging / Dev), time range (5m / 1h / 24h / 7d), search (⌘K), theme toggle, alert bell; four top KPIs (total requests / error rate / p95 / availability) with sparklines and period-over-period deltas; 24-card endpoint health grid (red cards first), each card with HTTP method + path + health dot + RPS / p95 / error rate; right alerts side panel with 8 active alerts and per-row assign / silence actions; bottom global p50 / p95 / p99 trend line chart. - `endpoint-detail.html` — Endpoint detail. Top: method + path + health badge + linked services + owner avatars; 6 KPIs (RPS / error rate / p50 / p95 / p99 / SLO status); three large trend charts (request volume, latency p50/p95/p99 three lines, error rate); error-grouping panel with status-code / client-version / region tabs; recent error sample table (5 rows including 502 Bad Gateway, 500, 429, 503); related traces list. - `alerts.html` — Alerts center. 4 KPIs (active / new today / mean response / MTTR); filter bar; 12-row alert

run_plan.goal: Explore the AeroIQ monitoring SaaS end-to-end with emphasis on the dashboard-to-detail investigation path, alert triage, endpoint filtering/search, and service topology navigation, while validating responsive/mobile usability on the same critical flows.
run_plan.summary: Start on the dashboard and verify the primary operational flow: understand system health, inspect high-risk endpoint cards, and drill into a detailed endpoint view. Then cover the adjacent operational pages—Endpoints, Alerts, and Service Map—using the visible filters, search, time range, environment, theme, and assignment/silence controls to confirm state changes and cross-page consistency. Repeat the most important navigation and triage checks in a mobile viewport, with special attention to small tap targets and unlabeled controls already flagged by prescan.
assumptions: The main workflow is dashboard-first, then drilldown into endpoint detail and alerts for incident investigation.

The visible page set in prescan is the full reachable scope for this run; Logs, Integrations, and Settings appear in nav but were not enumerated as separate HTML pages, so they should only be treated as navigation affordances if they resolve in-app.

The endpoint-detail page likely represents a single representative unhealthy endpoint rather than a list of all details, so coverage should focus on the shown error breakdown, sample table, and trace list rather than expecting editable workflow controls.
risk_hotspots: index.html: top-right org selector, environment tabs, and time-range buttons are small on mobile and one select lacks an accessible label.
index.html: Active Alerts side panel actions (Assign, Silence) and the alert bell badge may hide state or be hard to operate on smaller screens.
endpoints.html: service/health/tag filters and search field are key stateful controls; verify they update the list and do not break row alignment.
alerts.html: multiple filters plus the alerts table represent the highest triage complexity; watch for missing labels and selected-state clarity.
endpoint-detail.html: error-breakdown tabs and recent sample rows are likely the most information-dense and should be checked for tab switching, truncation, and readability.
services.html: the service map depends on node-click interactions; validate whether node selection is discoverable and whether the Production/Staging toggle changes the graph meaningfully.
mobile viewport across all pages: sidebar/nav links and primary toolbar controls are below recommended tap-target size.

phases.title: Dashboard orientation and state controls
phases.objective: Validate the landing dashboard, global navigation, and top-level state controls that anchor the rest of the exploration.
key_checks: Confirm the dashboard loads with the KPI row, endpoint health grid, active alerts panel, and global latency chart visible and coherent.
Exercise environment tabs (Production, Staging, Dev) and time ranges (5m, 1h, 24h, 7d) to check for visible state change or selected styling.
Use org switcher, theme toggle, notification bell, and profile button to confirm they are interactive and do not break layout.
Open at least one high-risk endpoint card from the health grid to verify drilldown path into endpoint detail.
exit_criteria: At least one environment/time-range combination has been toggled and the selected state observed.
One endpoint card or equivalent drill-in path has been followed to the detail page.
No blocking layout or interaction failures on the dashboard nav or key controls.

phases.title: Endpoint drilldown and incident evidence
phases.objective: Inspect the unhealthy endpoint detail page for depth of troubleshooting information and tabbed breakdown behavior.
key_checks: Validate the header context: method, path, health badge, linked services, owner, and SLO breach state.
Review the KPI strip and the three charts for request volume, latency, and error rate to ensure they read as distinct diagnostics.
Switch the error breakdown tabs (status code, client version, region) and verify each tab updates the breakdown content.
Inspect recent error samples for representative error classes (502, 500, 429, 503) and check truncation/row readability.
Open or inspect related traces to confirm the page supports deeper trace-level follow-up.
exit_criteria: All visible diagnostic sections have been viewed at least once.
At least one tab change in error breakdown has been confirmed.
The error sample table and trace list are readable and actionable.

phases.title: Endpoint catalog filtering and search
phases.objective: Validate the endpoints list as the broader navigation and filtering surface for the fleet.
key_checks: Confirm the endpoints table/list renders with service, health, RPS, p95, error %, SLO, deploy age, and owner columns or equivalents.
Use service, health, tag, and method/path search filters to narrow the list and confirm the results update predictably.
Check that unhealthy/degraded rows are distinguishable from healthy rows and that breach indicators are legible.
Select at least one row or endpoint path if linked, to verify a second path into endpoint detail or comparable drilldown.
exit_criteria: At least two different filter types have been exercised.
Search or filter results visibly change the list.
Row status styling and key columns remain understandable after filtering.

phases.title: Alert triage and resolution affordances
phases.objective: Validate the alerts center as the core operational triage flow, including filtering, table readability, and row-level actions.
key_checks: Check the KPI cards for active alerts, new today, mean response time, and MTTR.
Use severity, rules, assignee, and status controls to filter the table and confirm the visible alert set updates.
Inspect the alerts table for time, rule, endpoint, severity, status, and owner coverage, especially critical vs warning distinctions.
Test row-level or summary actions where present, and confirm Assign/Silence behavior is understandable and does not cause accidental loss of context.
Verify the visible search input and other controls remain usable and not confusingly labeled.
exit_criteria: Multiple alert filters have been exercised and reflected in the table.
At least one alert action or action affordance has been inspected.
Alert severity and status are clearly distinguishable in the filtered view.

phases.title: Topology comprehension and service switching
phases.objective: Validate the service map as a system-wide navigation aid and inspect whether environment toggles and node interaction are meaningful.
key_checks: Confirm the service map loads with node graph labels and the explanatory text about edge width/traffic.
Toggle Production and Staging and observe whether the graph changes or the selected state is clear.
Click at least one service node if interactive to verify discoverability of node-based drilldown.
Check that the map remains interpretable without a legend overload or ambiguous node labeling.
exit_criteria: At least one environment toggle on the service map has been tested.
A node interaction has been attempted or confirmed as non-blocking if unavailable.
The page remains readable at both desktop and mobile sizes.

phases.title: Mobile recheck of critical flows
phases.objective: Repeat the most important dashboard, alerts, and detail interactions in a mobile viewport to validate tap-targets, spacing, and preserved task flow.
key_checks: Revisit dashboard navigation, top controls, and at least one endpoint card on mobile.
Re-test alerts triage controls and one table row/action on mobile.
Re-check endpoint detail tab switching and sample readability on mobile.
Assess whether sidebar nav links, environment/time-range buttons, and org selector are still operable despite small tap targets.
Confirm whether the missing-label and small-target warnings materially hinder task completion.
exit_criteria: Critical flows can still be completed on mobile without blockers.
The most important small-target or unlabeled control issues have been confirmed as either minor or user-blocking.
Mobile results are captured for dashboard, alerts, and one detail page.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 5 known HTML pages and validate at least one meaningful interaction on each.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise the dashboard state controls, endpoint health drilldown, endpoint list filters/search, alert filters/actions, and service-map environment/node interactions.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the highest-value flows on mobile: dashboard controls, one endpoint detail drilldown, alerts filtering/action, and service-map environment toggling.

notes: Prescan already shows low-severity tap-target issues and at least one unlabeled select; prioritize confirming whether these are real mobile usability blockers.
No console or network errors were reported, so the run should focus on interaction quality, state clarity, and navigation depth rather than stability debugging.

ux_notes: Clicking the AeroIQ logo did not navigate away from the dashboard; the URL stayed on index.html, so the action did not expose a deeper incident-investigation path.
The dashboard content visibly refreshed in place, and the high-risk endpoint cards remain prominent in the endpoint health grid, but no new drilldown context was reached.
Low-severity tap-target warnings were present on several left-nav items, and the org selector was missing an accessible label, which may hinder navigation on smaller screens.

step.objective: Learn whether the endpoints list provides a better, more discoverable entry into endpoint investigation than the nonfunctional logo/dashboard item.
step.success_criteria: Navigation lands on endpoints.html and reveals a list or filter surface with meaningful endpoint browsing controls.

ux_notes: Navigation to the dedicated Endpoints page succeeded, replacing the dashboard with a purpose-built browsing surface.
The page provides stronger discovery than the dashboard item: filters for service, health, tag, and a search field are visible above a structured endpoint table.
The table exposes meaningful investigation columns at a glance (method, path, service, health, RPS, p95, error %, SLO, last deploy, owner), making endpoint triage much more discoverable.
No console or network errors were observed during the transition.

step.objective: Learn whether a representative unhealthy endpoint detail page provides clear diagnostic depth and switching behavior for incident investigation.
step.success_criteria: The detail page loads and exposes the endpoint header, KPI strip, diagnostic charts, tabbed error breakdown, and sample/trace sections for UX evaluation.

ux_notes: The endpoint detail page loaded cleanly with no console or network errors and exposes the expected diagnostic stack: header, KPI strip, three trend charts, tabbed error breakdown, recent error samples, and related traces.
The unhealthy state is explicit and actionable: `/v1/payments` is marked Unhealthy with SLO Breached, alongside high error rate and elevated p95/p99 latency, which supports incident triage.
Error breakdown tabs offer switching by status code, client version, and region; the current status-code view surfaces dominant 500/502/503/429 buckets, which is useful for narrowing causes.
Recent error samples provide concrete request IDs and messages, and the related traces list gives trace IDs with durations/spans, adding useful diagnostic depth beyond aggregate charts.
Mobile-oriented UX risk remains visible in the surrounding shell: several nav targets are under the 44px tap-size guidance, and the org select lacks a visible label/aria label.

step.objective: Learn how the alerts triage surface presents filtering, severity/status clarity, and row-level action affordances.

ux_notes: This action did not reach a mobile viewport; the dashboard reloaded in desktop mode, so mobile touch usability remains unverified.

On the observed desktop view, several primary navigation items are only 195×41px and below the 44px mobile tap-target guidance, suggesting likely touch-size issues if the same layout persists on mobile.
The org selector appears in the top bar without a visible label in the DOM summary, which is a medium accessibility/clarity concern for a control the user must notice and change.
Production, Staging, and time-range buttons are present and legible in the header; however, the layout still clusters many controls tightly, which may be cramped on smaller screens.

step.objective: Determine whether the dashboard’s primary controls and navigation remain usable at mobile size, especially the small environment/time-range controls and nav targets.
step.success_criteria: The browser should be in a mobile-sized state or otherwise clearly reveal mobile layout differences so tap-target usability can be assessed next.

The dashboard layout remained stable after the click; no console or network errors were reported.
